claims.text: In single-phase high-entropy alloys, toughness retention is governed by a balance between heterogeneous lattice strain and chemical short-range ordering or phase segregation.
Heterogeneous lattice strain causes unusual dislocation behavior, including multiple kinks or jogs and bidirectional cross-slip.
Lattice-strain-enabled dislocation behavior can underpin a strength-ductility synergy in distorted crystalline solids.
Nano-twinning provides an additional deformation mode that helps CrCoNi retain toughness despite high strength.
Uniformly distributed heterogeneous lattice strain promotes cross-slip and nano-twinning.
Cross-slip and nano-twinning dissipate energy at crack tips, provide crack-tip shielding, and inhibit crack propagation.
Chemical short-range order or segregation creates locally stiff regions.
Locally ordered or segregated regions hinder cross-slip and nano-twinning, reduce energy dissipation, and cause premature crack propagation and toughness loss.
The initial CrCoNi alloy is single-phase FCC.
Standard-processed or as-cast CrCoNi naturally contains heterogeneous lattice-strain fields and some local chemical order while retaining moderate toughness.
A homogenizing heat treatment combined with approximately 1–1.5 at.% Pd will reduce short-range order and modify the local lattice-strain distribution.
The heat-treated, Pd-modified alloy will have higher fracture toughness than the baseline alloy.
The heat-treated, Pd-modified alloy will exhibit more spatially uniform activation of dislocation slip, cross-slip, and nano-twinning than the baseline.
Regions with excessive short-range order in the baseline alloy will correlate with early crack initiation.
The proposed mechanism applies from room temperature to approximately 800°C in single-phase FCC high-entropy alloys.
The proposed mechanism may not apply outside the stated temperature range or to multiphase alloys.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant improvement exceeding 10% in KIC, or failure to observe enhanced deformation mechanisms, is specified as a falsifying result.
